title: Add Taildrop receiver toggle to Tailscale panel
head: 6d1b74d4d77e
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Combined with open accessibility PR #13212, the new switch fails its repository-wide naming test
leads.consequence: #13212 names the existing Tailscale switch and adds a scanner that requires a nonempty accessibleName/tooltipText/label on every ToggleSwitch under shell/plugins. This PR adds a second unnamed switch. The shell-only portions of #13212's diff apply to this PR's head without rejects or conflict markers; their test exits 1 naming shell/plugins/panels/tailscale/Panel.qml:544 ToggleSwitch. If merged without updating the new switch, test/shell fails and, once Quickshell exposes accessibility, the receiver switch has no spoken name. Supply accessibleName: "Receive files automatically" alongside the new switch when integrating #13212. The other PR's manual/ patch needs separate reconciliation against this branch; the test result is for its merged shell and test files.
leads.triage: factual, confirmed by coordinator reading coord/13212.diff ui-accessibility-test.sh required_names ToggleSwitch; new switch Panel.qml:541-546 has no name; Opus also confirmed by source

leads.summary: Clicking On can enable the receiver while the unit cannot run
leads.consequence: When the bar plugin is enabled manually but /usr/bin/tailscale is absent, the packaged unit exists and is-active returns 3, so the switch stays visible even though the panel reports Tailscale not installed. enable --now creates a persistent user .wants symlink, but ConditionPathExists=/usr/bin/tailscale skips start without a failed state. The toggle handler announces 'turned on' and flips the knob temporarily; the 300ms refresh returns inactive and flips it back, leaving the unit enabled so it can start after the binary appears. Separate availability from active/installed status, and confirm both desired state and enablement before success; do not present a usable On switch when its prerequisite cannot run.

leads.summary: Receiver switch cannot be reached from the keyboard-driven panel
leads.consequence: The new ToggleSwitch responds only to its MouseArea.onClicked; the panel moves its keyboard cursor through header/auth/accounts/exit nodes/peers and Enter always activates the selected existing action. Tab changes panels and there is no new shortcut. Keyboard-only users can see but cannot change automatic receiving. Add a receiver cursor section or a documented shortcut, with keyboard activation calling the same toggle. No compositor session was allocated, so this conclusion follows from the panel's event handlers rather than a live keypress.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; coordinator verified hasCursor on all other ToggleSwitch users

leads.summary: User-systemd/DBus query errors are misclassified as missing receiver unit
leads.consequence: is-active returns code 4 for a unit that does not exist, 3 for an existing inactive/failed/activating unit, and a nonzero error if the user manager cannot be reached. The code treats every result except 0/3 as receiverAvailable=false, hides the entire switch and never records stderr or lastError. During a manager/DBus outage, the user sees no indication that checking failed, cannot distinguish outage from missing unit, and the row reappears only on a successful future poll. Preserve a visible unavailable/error state and surface an actionable diagnostic rather than using an exit code alone as availability.
leads.triage: confirmed by Opus harness (nobus) but judged acceptable behaviour; dropped

leads.summary: Reinstalling Tailscale turns automatic receiving back on after the user opted out
leads.consequence: Turning Off disables the user unit persistently, but running the stock Tailscale service installer again unconditionally executes systemctl --user enable --now for that same unit and re-enables receiving. The panel's Off preference is therefore not durable across reinstall; the user may again receive files automatically after an operation they did not intend to opt in to receiving. If this is intentional reset behavior, document it; otherwise avoid re-enabling an explicitly disabled unit on reinstall or track explicit preference separately. Initial install and migration already enable by design.

leads.summary: A failed Process launch never fires either new onExited handler
leads.consequence: If systemctl cannot be launched, Quickshell's FailedToStart handler emits runningChanged but no exited signal. A failed status launch leaves receiverAvailable at its initial true/receiverActive false, inviting a click with unknown state; a failed toggle launch leaves 'Turning automatic file receiving on/off...' displayed without the success/error branch or delayed confirmation, and the switch can be clicked again after running becomes false. Handle Process start failures or add an independent timeout/error path; do not assume onExited always fires.
leads.triage: systemctl always present on target; negligible; dropped

leads.summary: Open PR #13353 changes image previews to glyphs and conflicts with this PR's new README paragraph
leads.consequence: #13353 replaces image-preview notifications with glyph-only notifications while this PR's rewritten receiving paragraph still promises an image preview. Both PRs independently replace the same original README lines; a three-way merge at the common base yields a real content conflict. Resolve with text preserving this PR's switch description and #13353's glyph behavior; do not keep the preview claim after merging #13353. #13353 is diverged, not stacked; GitHub lists it mergeable into quattro independently.
leads.triage: factual, confirmed by coordinator (coord/13353.diff rewrites same paragraph) and Opus git apply --check

leads.summary: New receiving copy promises ~/Downloads even if the receiver is configured for a different directory
leads.consequence: The existing receiver selects ${XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR:-$HOME/Downloads} unless given an explicit directory. If XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR is exported to a different path (or a user-supplied unit overrides the ExecStart directory), the On subtitle 'New files go to Downloads' and the rewritten README's ~/Downloads promise can misdirect users looking for delivered files. Related open #12023 (diverged) adds xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD support even when the env var is absent, broadening the mismatch if it merges. Describe the configured downloads directory, or avoid claiming a literal ~/Downloads destination.
leads.triage: default is ~/Downloads (bin/omarchy-tailscale-receive:15); pre-existing README wording; dropped

leads.summary: Manual's two Tailscale panel guides do not mention how to turn automatic receiving off
leads.consequence: Both manual sections enumerate the panel's actions; networking still states that received files land automatically in ~/Downloads with no qualification. Users reading the shipped manual will not discover the new opt-out control and may infer receiving is unconditional. Add the switch and the disabled-state caveat to those two sections, particularly the networking receiving paragraph.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus optional note; omitted from public comment as minor

leads.summary: New tests assert command strings exist but never execute the receiver toggle
leads.consequence: The added tests would pass with a plausible broken implementation where toggleReceiver starts with `if (true) return` while preserving the command arrays and Panel.onToggled string: no receiver action would run and the static .includes checks would still pass. Add a unit/QML contract test of click -> process invocation, exit-code handling and status refresh, ideally with a stub systemctl and checked command argv/exit outputs. Head tailscale-test and qml-text-format-test passed under LC_ALL=C; newly-added source-string assertions fail as expected when transplanted onto the merge-base, so the weakness is fidelity, not failure to distinguish the old source.

leads.summary: Receiver probe starts on every timer tick even when Tailscale is not installed
leads.consequence: On a machine with the Tailscale plugin on the bar but no tailscale binary, refresh() still starts systemctl --user is-active before probing installed, including every 2 seconds for up to 30 seconds at startup and every 30 seconds thereafter by default. The unit is shipped to all Omarchy installations but the receiver cannot start without the binary, so the extra DBus process never answers a useful question there; guard the probe behind the installed/prerequisite state or stop polling when absent until install/reopen. This is a small idle-process cost, not an assertion about an unmeasured performance regression.
leads.triage: factual; initially folded into F1 suggestion, removed after Opus self-check D3 (plain !installed return would skip startup poll)

Behavioral claims use pinned project files and upstream systemd v257/Quickshell source; the exact installed systemd version is not pinned by omarchy's package recipe. # RETRO: PR #11978 (team 4)

## What worked
- Parallel Opus review and Sol hunt: Sol independently found both Opus low findings and added two related-PR conflicts (#13212 lint, #13353 README) that Opus had not covered.
- Opus runtime harness (real Service.qml under Quickshell with stubbed systemctl modelled on systemd source) gave concrete timings for the condition-skip finding.
- Self-check caught 7 real wording errors (position "under" vs "above", "never cleared", loose commit attribution, incomplete poll suggestion, "single systemctl call").

## Process deviations
1. Coordinator saw Sol's one-line headline (the #13212 lead) in the `pi_job.py wait` output before Opus's final was saved. Not passed to Opus; no contamination of Opus's independent report. Suggest `wait` suppress `latest_text` until release.
2. Opus used `ls -la` on its own fixture directory (owner-name resolution); brief requires `ls -1` or `ls -lan`.
3. Opus ran one unstubbed Quickshell probe inside review.py (rv-qsprobe) that invoked the host-installed `tailscale` binary and `systemctl --user is-active` in the sandbox. Private /run, /home and network meant neither daemon was reachable; result excluded from conclusions. The brief's "no tailscale commands against the host" was intended to cover this; future briefs should say "stub every external command before loading Service.qml".
4. Opus's report Write was refused by the harness; handback saved with save-handback (expected, not a deviation).

## Carry forward
- For QML service reviews, the stubbed-Quickshell harness pattern is effective; brief it explicitly.
- Sol's related-open-PR checks are worth keeping; verify lint claims by reading the other PR's test.
comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** With Tailscale installed, the switch tracks the receiver unit and toggles it as described. `systemctl --user is-active` exit 0 shows the switch on, and exit 3 (inactive, failed or activating) shows it off. A missing unit (exit 4) or an unreachable user manager hides the row. A successful `enable --now` / `disable --now` flips the switch, and the 300 ms follow-up check confirms the state. Repeated toggles while one is running produce a single enable/disable command. The commands match the ones used by `omarchy-install-service-tailscale`, `omarchy-remove-service-tailscale` and migration `1785101000`, and the diff applies cleanly to current `quattro`.

Two small issues remain, plus notes on tests and related open PRs.

### Receiver row appears when Tailscale is not installed

The row is gated only on `receiverAvailable` (`Panel.qml:511-547`), while the power switch uses `visible: tailscale.installed`. The receive unit ships with every install, so `is-active` returns 3 even without the Tailscale CLI. The switch then shows up above "Tailscale CLI is not installed or not on PATH."

Turning it on in that state "succeeds": the unit's `ConditionPathExists=/usr/bin/tailscale` makes systemd skip the start without an error, so `enable --now` exits 0.

```text
click switch (Tailscale CLI absent)
  systemctl --user enable --now omarchy-tailscale-receive.service   -> exit 0 (start skipped by condition)
  panel: "Automatic file receiving turned on", switch on
  +300 ms  is-active -> 3                                           -> switch back off, message still "turned on"
  result: unit left enabled, receiver not running
```

If the command fails instead, "Could not change automatic file receiving" stays until a later toggle succeeds, because no Tailscale status refresh runs while the CLI is absent.

**Impact:** Limited. The bar widget is normally present only for Tailscale users, since the install script enables it, the remove script disables it and bar defaults add it only when Tailscale is installed. It still shows a confusing control to anyone who added the widget manually or removed Tailscale with pacman.

**Suggested change:** Use `visible: tailscale.installed && tailscale.receiverAvailable` for the separator and row, and add `!installed` to the guard in `toggleReceiver()`.

### New switch cannot be reached from the keyboard

The panel's cursor sections (`header`, `auth`, `accounts`, `exitNodes`, `peers`) and text keys (`t`, `c`, `n`, `d`, `s`) never reach the new `ToggleSwitch` (`Panel.qml:541-546`), and it has no `hasCursor` binding. Every other `ToggleSwitch` under `shell/plugins` binds `hasCursor`, and 228b5ac3 ("Give every hero toggle a keyboard focus ring") made the panel toggles keyboard-reachable.

**Impact:** In a panel otherwise operated with j/k and Enter, the receiver setting is mouse-only.

**Suggested change:** Add a receiver section after `header` in `ensureCursor`, `moveCursor` and `activateCursor`, and bind `hasCursor` and `onHovered` the way the power switch does.

**Optional test improvement:** The new assertions in `tailscale-test.sh` check that the strings exist. They fail on the base as expected, but in a mutation check they still passed with the enable/disable commands swapped, with the `is-active` mapping inverted, or with `refreshReceiver()` removed from `refresh()`. Moving the exit-code mapping (0, 3, 4, other) and the command choice into `Model.js` would let the existing node tests check that behavior directly.

**Optional:** `receiverToggleProcess` collects no stdout or stderr, so a failure only shows the generic message. The service's other actions show `stderr || stdout || fallback`.

**Related open PRs:** #13212 adds a lint requiring every `ToggleSwitch` under `shell/plugins` to have an `accessibleName`, `tooltipText` or `label`, and, of the Tailscale panel's switches, names only the existing power switch. The new switch has none of these, so whichever PR merges second needs something like `accessibleName: "Receive files automatically"`. #13353 also rewrites the same "Receiving files" README paragraph, so the two README edits will conflict.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the head commit and the related user unit, scripts and migration. `tailscale-test.sh` and `qml-text-format-test.sh` were run in an isolated sandbox at head, at the base and with the diff applied to current `quattro`. The PR's `Service.qml` ran under Quickshell 0.3.1 (offscreen) with `systemctl` and `tailscale` stubbed to follow systemd 261's `is-active` and `enable`/`disable` exit codes, which were read from source. No real user service manager, compositor or visual check was involved, and `./test/all` was not run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
